title: Cancer Cell CD73 Loss Promotes a Dual Inflammatory and Immunosuppressive Microenvironment in Endometrial Carcinoma

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《Cancer Cell CD73 Loss Promotes a Dual Inflammatory and Immunosuppressive Microenvironment in Endometrial Carcinoma》：研究问题的原文依据。

【Introduction · s1-p2】Increasing evidence suggests that immune evasion is important not only to high-grade endometrial carcinomas but also to disease progression in low-grade tumors (6–8). Low-grade (grade 1 and 2) endometrioid endometrial carcinomas (EEC) are the most common endometrial carcinoma subtype. Although most patients present with early-stage disease and favorable prognosis, approximately 5% to 10% experience recurrence and poor survival outcomes (6). One possible explanation for the aggressiveness of these tumors is the gain of mechanisms that promote immunosuppression (6, 7). Although CD73 is downregulated in high-grade EECs and endometrial serous carcinomas, CD73 expression in low-grade EECs is highly variable, ranging from levels comparable with normal endometrium to near complete loss (3). Conceivably, this variability may reflect different pathobiologies. Low-grade EECs are one of the most diverse groups of endometrial tumors in terms of genetic and molecular features (9–11). Considering the variability of CD73 expression and the strong link of CD73 to immunosuppression in other solid tumors, we sought to determine whether CD73 has a role in the immunobiology of low-grade EECs.

【Introduction · s1-p1】CD73, a cell surface 5′ nucleotidase that generates extracellular adenosine, is a well-established mediator of immunosuppression in cancer. Extracellular adenosine is immunosuppressive in both normal and cancerous tissues, and many tumors upregulate CD73 to evade antitumor immune cell responses (1, 2). Small-molecule inhibitors and antibodies that inhibit CD73 are currently being evaluated in clinical trials, often in combination with immune checkpoint blockade or chemotherapy (1, 2). CD73 expression differs in endometrial carcinomas. Rather than being overexpressed, CD73 is frequently downregulated in high-grade endometrial tumors, and its loss is associated with prognostically poor clinical features and worse survival outcomes (3). Similar associations between CD73 loss and adverse clinical features or poor prognosis have been reported in prostate and bladder cancers (4, 5). Although tumor-promoting functions of CD73 are well-understood, why some tumors downregulate CD73 remains largely unknown. As targeted therapy for CD73 continues to advance, understanding CD73–adenosine biology in cancers with more diverse expression will be critical for personalized treatment strategies.

sections.title: 研究方法
sections.text:
《Cancer Cell CD73 Loss Promotes a Dual Inflammatory and Immunosuppressive Microenvironment in Endometrial Carcinoma》：方法与研究设计的原文依据。

【Stromal cell CD73 expression does not associate with clinical features or patient outcomes · s3-3-p1】We next determined whether strong stromal cell CD73 expression was associated with clinical outcomes. Tumors were supervised by percent stromal staining 2+ and divided into three groups based on quartiles (Supplementary Fig. S6A and S6B). Tumors with the highest percentage of stromal cells (≥55.16%) with strong CD73 staining (Stromal Cell Group 3) did not associate with poor clinical features or patient outcomes compared with tumors with a low percentage (≤5.46%; Stromal Cell Group 1) of stromal staining 2+ (Supplementary Fig. S6C–S6E). Although CD73 cancer cell loss correlates with a higher likelihood of strong stromal CD73 expression (Fig. 1B), these data show that increased stromal expression is not driving poor clinical features or patient outcomes. Rather, loss of cancer cell CD73 is the major contributor to these clinical endpoints.

【Loss of cancer cell CD73 is associated with increased LVSI and worse patient outcomes · s3-2-p1】With cancer and stromal cells having distinct CD73 expression patterns, we first assessed the clinical relevance of CD73 cancer cell expression. Tumors were supervised by percent “no staining” for CD73 in the cancer cells and divided into groups based on quartiles (Fig. 1A–C). Cancer Cell Group 3 represents tumors with the greatest loss of cancer cell CD73 expression, and Cancer Cell Group 1 represents tumors with little to no loss (≤1.15%; Fig. 1A–C). Loss of cancer cell CD73 expression in G2 EECMSS (Cancer Cell Group 3) was associated with lymphovascular space invasion (LVSI; Fig. 1D; Supplementary Fig. S5) and worse survival outcomes (Fig. 1E and F) compared with tumors having little to no loss of cancer cell CD73 expression (Cancer Cell Group 1). These data are similar to CD73 downregulation in high-grade endometrial carcinoma (3) and suggest that loss of cancer cell CD73 is essential for tumor progression in low-grade endometrial carcinoma. LVSI is an independent risk factor for recurrence and worse outcomes in low-risk, early-stage endometrial carcinomas (22) and has been recently linked to immune and inflammatory changes within the tumor microenvironment (23).

sections.title: 主要结果
sections.text:
《Cancer Cell CD73 Loss Promotes a Dual Inflammatory and Immunosuppressive Microenvironment in Endometrial Carcinoma》：结果的原文依据；数值与适用人群以引文为准。

【Single-cell RNA-seq analysis · s2-11-p1】Canonical correlation analysis was used to integrate data from different patients. For quality control, only cells with more than 200 and less than 7,500 genes expressed and less than 10% mitochondrial counts were retained. In total, 7,114 cells were used for downstream analyses after the quality control. For finding clusters using Seurat, 20 dimensions of reduction and 0.5 resolution were used. A Uniform Manifold Approximation and Projection (UMAP) plot was also generated using the 20 dimensions of reduction by Seurat (RRID: SCR_016341). The R package cellassign (version 0.99; RRID: SCR_025986) was used to perform cell type assignment. Marker genes used for cell type assignment can be found in Cochrane and colleagues (15). The R package clusterProfiler was used for GO enrichment analysis for the marker genes in each cluster.

【Loss of cancer cell CD73 defines a distinct inflamed tumor phenotype characterized by active T-cell infiltration coupled with adaptive immune suppression · s3-6-p1】To independently validate that tumors with CD73 loss were more likely to have increased PD-L1, we examined PD-L1 protein expression in our G2 EECMSS IHC cohort (Fig. 1). Consistent with CD274 expression in the TCGA-UCEC data for G2 EECMSS in Fig. 3C, we found that tumors with cancer cell CD73 loss (no staining) showed a higher percentage of PD-L1–positive cancer cells, whereas tumors with high membrane + cytoplasm CD73 staining exhibited lower PD-L1 expression (Fig. 4A). These data were secondarily confirmed using the Cancer Cell Groups described in Fig. 1C. Tumors with a high percent of cancer cell CD73 loss (Cancer Cell Group 3) were more likely to have an increased percentage of cancer cells expressing PD-L1 (PD-L1 >1% and PD-L1 >2%; Fig. 4B). Together, these data support a link between cancer cell CD73 loss and tumor-intrinsic immune checkpoint upregulation in low-grade EECs.

sections.title: 图表阅读
sections.text:
《Cancer Cell CD73 Loss Promotes a Dual Inflammatory and Immunosuppressive Microenvironment in Endometrial Carcinoma》：图表的原始标题与说明。

【Figure 1. · fig1】Figure 1. Loss of cancer cell CD73 is associated with aggressive clinical features and poor outcomes. A, Expression mapping of CD73 IHC staining categories in cancer and stromal cells across 119 individual G2 EECMSS. Tumors are ordered by decreasing percentage of cancer cell area lacking CD73 staining. Cancer cell staining categories include membrane + cytoplasm staining, membrane downregulation with cytoplasmic staining, and no staining. Stromal CD73 staining is categorized as no staining, stromal staining 1+, or stromal staining 2+. B, Spearman correlations comparing CD73 staining patterns in cancer and stromal compartments. Circle color indicates Spearman rho, circle size reflects correlation strength, and asterisks indicate significance (*, P < 0.05; ***, P < 0.001). C, Tumors were stratified into three groups based on quartiles of cancer cell CD73-negative (no staining) area: Group 1, low/no CD73 loss (≤1.15%; n = 30); Group 2, intermediate CD73 loss (1.19%–25.68%; n = 59); and Group 3, high CD73 loss (32.38%–100%; n = 30). The plot displays the distribution of tumors according to the percentage of cancer cell area lacking CD73 staining. Each point represents an individual tumor; the x-axis indicates the percentage of cancer cell area with no CD73 staining, and the y-axis represents individual tumors ranked by CD73-negative (no staining) area. D, Association of CD73 loss with clinicopathologic features comparing Group 1 and Group 3. Features include myometrial invasion, stage, LVSI, and lymph node (LN) metastasis. Bar plots show number of tumors (tumor counts). The Fisher exact test was used for group comparisons, and ORs were calculated using the Baptista–Pike method. CI, confidence interval. E and F, Recurrence-free and overall survival comparisons in Group 1 vs. Group 3 by the log-rank (Mantel–Cox) test; P values shown. D–F, Information for clinical features, recurrence-free survival, or overall survival was not available for all tumors.

【Figure 2. · fig2】Figure 2. Loss of CD73 is associated with increased pro-inflammatory cytokine/chemokine expression. A, Volcano plot showing DEGs in 50 G2 EECMSS from TCGA-UCEC stratified by low vs. high NT5E expression. NT5E-low and -high were defined by the lower and upper quartiles, respectively. Red and blue dots indicate genes upregulated and downregulated in NT5E-low cases. B, GO analysis of DEGs in NT5E-low vs. NT5E-high tumors. BP, CC, and MF indicate GO Biological Process, Cellular Component, and Molecular Function categories, respectively. C, KEGG pathway enrichment analysis of genes upregulated or downregulated in NT5E-low cases. Upregulated pathways include cytokine–cytokine receptor interaction and chemokine signaling. D, STRING protein–protein interaction network of genes within the cytokine–cytokine receptor interaction pathway identified in C. Annotations, indicated by colored circles, are associated immune signaling pathways. E, GO Biological Process (BP) enrichment analysis of the 15 cytokine–cytokine receptor interaction genes identified in C, showing particular enrichment of neutrophil and lymphocyte chemotaxis and chemokine-mediated signaling.

【Figure 3. · fig3】Figure 3. Pro-inflammatory cytokine/chemokine expression correlates with increased PD-L1 and immunosuppression gene expression in NT5E-low tumors. A–C, Spearman correlations of CD274 (PD-L1) vs. the 15 cytokine–cytokine receptor interaction genes identified in Fig. 2C. Correlations are shown in G2 EECMSS for (A) all tumors, (B) NT5E-high tumors, and (C) NT5E-low tumors. NT5E-low and -high tumors were those defined by the lower and upper quartiles in Fig. 2A. D, Spearman correlations of immunosuppression genes vs. the 15 cytokine–cytokine receptor interaction genes identified in Fig. 2C in NT5E-high and NT5E-low cases. The list of immunosuppressive genes was from Harmonizome 3.0, Immunosuppression. E, STRING protein–protein interaction network of immunosuppressive genes with ≥3 significant correlations, corresponding to genes highlighted in red or blue in D, clustered by K-means. *, P < 0.05; **, P < 0.009; ***, P < 0.0009.
